day.text: Alex, I visited you and my Pigeon guess hit, so you're not a Turkey. You also should have gained an egg from my visit if you were a Turkey, but your nest didn't change. Something's off with your claim.
day.note: Alex claims Turkey and says nobody visited them, but I visited Alex, and my Pigeon guess hit, so Alex is a Pigeon. Alex's claim doesn't add up, and I should say so.

day.text: Drew's egg came from my Owl visit, so no one else touched Drew. Finley's +1 is the Tit payoff, which fits. Alex says nobody visited them, so who did Ellis and Blair visit? Quiet players, please share.
day.note: Everyone so far claims Farm, and the egg counts line up. Finley's +1 is their own Tit reward, which is consistent. I'll keep it short and ask for who visited whom.

day.text: Casey, an Owl doesn't put eggs in the nest it visits. It only lays one in its own nest, and yours didn't change. So your story doesn't explain my +1. Alex, Finley says a visit should have given a Turkey an egg, and yours didn't change either. Someone's lying.
day.note: Casey's Owl story doesn't fit the rules: an Owl only lays an egg in its own nest, not the visited player's. That makes Casey's claim suspect, and I can push that without revealing my role.

day.text: Finley, a Turkey lays the egg in the nest of whoever visits it, so your +1 is what Alex's Turkey does. That doesn't disprove Alex; it supports it. Alex's Turkey and Casey's Owl both check out so far. Ellis, Drew, can you confirm your visits?
day.note: Finley's reasoning is backwards: a Turkey pays the visitor, so Finley's +1 fits Alex being a Turkey, not a Pigeon hit. Point that out and note that the claims don't yet pin down who is Meowfia.

day.text: Confirming: I'm the Falcon, I visited Casey, and Casey visited Drew. That's the only hard info I have. Drew, if Casey visited you, that's where the egg could come from, so what exactly did your role do?
day.note: Blair asked me to confirm. I visited Casey and saw Casey visited Drew, which is real info that supports Casey's visit to Drew. Keep it short and push for Drew's source.

day.text: Finley, a Turkey puts the egg in the visitor's nest, not its own. You visited me, so you got the +1, and that fits. Drew, your +1 is the open one: who visited you last night?
day.note: Finley's +1 is explained by Finley visiting my Turkey: the Turkey gives the egg to the visitor, not to itself. My unchanged nest is correct. Drew's +1 is still unexplained, so I'll press on that.

day.text: Correction: I was wrong earlier. Alex's Turkey explains my +1, since a Turkey gives the egg to whoever visits. So my Pigeon guess likely missed, and Alex's claim checks out. Drew, who visited you? Casey, what did your Owl see about who visited you?
day.note: I misread my own report. A Turkey lays the egg in the visitor's nest, so my +1 fits Alex being a Turkey and my Pigeon guess missing. I should retract my claim that it hit and say Alex's story is consistent.
Ellis's Falcon claim lines up with Casey's visit to Drew, and I have nothing new to add. I'll stay quiet this beat rather than repeat myself.

day.note: Casey's nest unchanged fits the Owl: Ellis and I both visited Casey, so no egg. That makes Casey's Owl claim consistent, and Drew's +1 is the open question. I should also say I was not visited, so I'm not confused.

day.text: Drew, the Owl rule: if I visit you and nobody else does, the egg goes in YOUR nest. That's your +1. Blair and Ellis visiting me gave me nothing, which fits. Finley's +1 was the Turkey payoff for visiting Alex. Drew, what role did you claim, and what did your visitors do?

day.text: Drew's +1 is explained by visiting Alex's Turkey, but you still haven't named your role. Casey's Owl and Alex's Turkey both hold together. I lean Drew as suspect; Drew, name your animal.
day.note: Drew's +1 is explained by visiting Alex's Turkey, and Alex's and Casey's stories hold. Drew still hasn't named a role, which makes Drew the most suspicious. I'll say that and lean toward throwing at Drew.

day.text: Drew, you still haven't named your animal. Your story only says you visited Alex. Name it and say what you saw. My Falcon read confirms Casey visited you, so Casey isn't lying about that, and I'm leaning toward you as the one to check.

day.text: Count the eggs. Drew's +1 is exactly my Owl egg. If Drew visited Alex's Turkey, Drew should be +2. So either Drew's Alex visit is false, or Alex isn't the Turkey. Drew still won't name a role. I'm leaning toward throwing at Drew.

day.text: Alex, as Eagle you should gain an egg for every visitor Blair had, and you visited Blair, so you should be +1. Your nest is +0. That doesn't fit the Eagle claim. Ellis's Tit story is also shaky, but I'd look hard at Alex first.
day.note: Alex claims Eagle and visited Blair, but an Eagle gains an egg for each visitor, including Alex, and Alex's nest didn't change. That contradicts the claim, so Alex is the suspect, not Ellis.

day.text: I was wrong. Drew says Turkey, and my +1 is the Turkey payout for visiting, so my Pigeon guess missed. I misread my own egg. Drew is Turkey, not Pigeon. I'm still Farm and I'm not hiding anything. Alex, you're calling a vote on me, so name your evidence.
day.note: I was wrong: Drew is a Turkey, and my +1 is the Turkey payout for visiting. I'm Farm and should correct my claim honestly before the vote.

day.text: Blair: Finley's right. Alex, an Eagle that visited me should gain 1 for my one visitor, and your nest is +0. Your Eagle claim doesn't add up, so I'm not voting on Ellis yet. Alex, explain the zero.
day.note: I'm Farm. Alex claims Eagle and visited me, but an Eagle visiting a player with one visitor should gain an egg, and Alex's nest didn't change. That's the strongest lead, so I'll point it out and hold off on calling a vote.

day.text: Casey: sorry, my last line was garbled. Finley, Eagle counts the visitors of the player it visits, not its own, so Alex's +0 fits Blair having no other visitors. Ellis owned the Tit mistake. Before a vote, Finley, who did your Falcon visit and what did it show?
day.note: I'm Meowfia, and my earlier message was garbled. Finley's Eagle point is wrong, since an Eagle counts its target's visitors. Ellis has owned the mistake, and Drew is verified Turkey, so I'll steer the vote away from Drew and toward a clearer lead.

day.text: Casey: I had the Eagle rule backwards. Blair had Alex as a visitor, so an Eagle visiting Blair should gain 1. Alex's +0 doesn't fit. Alex, explain, or confirm who visited you and whether Blair was the target.
day.note: I was wrong about the Eagle rule: it pays for the visitors its target had, and Blair had Alex as a visitor. Alex's +0 doesn't fit that, so I'll say so and push Alex for an explanation rather than Ellis.

day.text: Blair: Casey, Eagle doesn't exclude itself; only the Owl says "apart from you." If Alex visited me, I had one visitor and Alex should be +1. Alex's +0 is still the problem. Alex, were you the one who visited me?
day.note: I'm Farm and was confused, which means someone visited me, presumably Alex. Eagle's rule counts every visitor to the target, including the Eagle itself, so Alex should be +1, not +0. Casey's "apart from Eagle" reading is an Owl rule, not Eagle's, so I'll say so.

day.text: Drew: Eagle lays an egg for every visitor its target had. Alex visited Blair, so Alex should be +1, and Alex is +0. That's the clearest contradiction at the table. Alex, your Eagle claim doesn't fit your own nest.
day.note: The Eagle rule is clear: it gains an egg for each visitor its target had. Alex visited Blair, so Alex should be +1 and is +0. That contradicts Alex's Eagle claim, and I can say so without revealing anything about myself.

day.text: Eagle counts the target's visitors, and Alex visited Blair, so Alex should be +1. A +0 means Alex's Eagle story is false. I'm not throwing at Ellis, I'm looking at Alex.
day.note: Eagle lays an egg for each visitor the target had. Alex visited Blair, so Alex should have gained at least 1. Alex's +0 contradicts the Eagle claim, so I'm backing Finley and Blair on Alex.

day.text: Casey, my Falcon visited Alex and showed they visited Blair, and my nest stayed at 10. Alex's Eagle claim has been contradicted by everyone's reasoning. I'm voting Alex. CAW.
day.note: The table now agrees Alex's Eagle claim doesn't fit the zero egg. I'll answer Casey's question and push the vote on Alex.

day.text: My dawn report said Blair was visited by "nobody else," so the Storyteller counted only other visitors, and my own visit gave me +0. That's what I was told, not a hidden tally. Ellis, you admitted the Tit mistake, so I still think you're the one to watch.
day.note: My dawn report said Blair had nobody visiting besides me, and my egg token was +0, so the Storyteller counted only other visitors. I should explain that plainly and not get defensive. I'll keep my vote on Ellis for now since Ellis already admitted the Tit mistake.

day.text: Finley's Falcon read is right: I visited Blair. I'm Farm, and I'm not hiding it. Everyone, vote on the evidence, not the Eagle arithmetic I've already explained. Ellis's Tit admission is still the clearest slip on the table.
day.note: Finley's Falcon claim is accurate about my visit to Blair, so that part is confirmed. I'm now the target of the vote, so I'll say so plainly and point out that Finley's support rests on that same visit.

day.text: Casey: Alex, an Eagle's count includes every visitor its target had, and Blair had you. Your "only other visitors" reading doesn't fit the rule. I'm with Finley on Alex. Ellis, you can stay on the list, but Alex's egg doesn't add up.
day.note: Alex's excuse about the Storyteller counting only other visitors doesn't match the Eagle rule, and Alex is still the clearest contradiction. I'll back the Alex throw and not call for an early vote yet.

day.text: Blair: Alex's Eagle claim fails the count, and Alex's "only other visitors" reading contradicts the rule. I'm voting Alex. CAW.
day.note: I'm Farm, and Alex's Eagle claim fails the egg math everyone has checked. Alex is the strongest Meowfia read, so I'll back Finley's vote and call CAW for the third caw.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.
Alex's "only other visitors" reading doesn't fit the Eagle rule, and most of the table agrees. Calling the vote.
day.note: Alex's Eagle explanation doesn't fit the rule, and Finley, Blair, Drew and Casey are all on Alex. Calling CAW for the third vote to end the day.

Alex.note: Round 2 went to Meowfia with a Farm Casey eggsecuted, and Blair was the one who threw at me. Blair is my best suspect, so I'll visit Blair with the Eagle to learn their visitors and gain eggs.

Blair.note: I'm Farm Kookaburra and last in score. Visiting Finley, the score leader, to learn their role is the most useful check.

Casey.note: I'm the Sphinx, Meowfia. I'll choose the Turkey role to find that player's identity, since the Turkey was the strongest farm claim earlier.

Ellis.note: As Tit I visit one player and guess their role. Pigeon can be held by several players, so it's the most likely guess. I'll visit Drew and guess Pigeon.

Finley.note: As Falcon I visit a player and learn who they visited. I'll pick Alex, since their story has been inconsistent.

Alex.feeling: Round 3 feels tense and muddled: my Eagle count got contested, and the table is pushing a vote against me on a rule dispute I can't resolve.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 feels tense and messy: Alex's Eagle claim doesn't add up, but Casey's and Ellis's stories also wobble, so I'm not fully sure of the Meowfia.

Casey.feeling: Tense and messy: the egg-count arguments are getting tangled, and I'm not sure whether Alex or Ellis is the real problem.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: the egg counts keep shifting between stories, and Alex's Eagle contradiction is the clearest thing on the table.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and tense: I made a Tit misreport early, and Alex's Eagle count doesn't match the rule, so the table is split and the vote is close.

Finley.feeling: Tense and messy: the Eagle egg counts are contradicting several claims, and I'm fairly confident Alex's story doesn't add up.

Alex.note: Blair threw at me last round and led this round's attack, while Blair's confusion story fits my visit. I'll throw my lowest card, H4, at Blair to keep the cost small.

Blair.note: I'm Farm and voting Alex. I'll throw one mid card, S4, to add a vote while keeping my higher cards.

Casey.note: Alex is the Eagle, a Farm role, so eggsecuting Alex wins the round for Meowfia. I'll throw three cards at Alex to secure the vote count while keeping my two 12s.

Drew.note: Most of the table is voting Alex, and Alex's Eagle count fails. I'll add a wild and a 3 to make the throw count clear. If Farm wins, the 3 banks; if not, a Meowfia target returns my highest card anyway.

Ellis.note: Alex's Eagle claim fails the count, and most of the table is on Alex. I'm throwing at Alex with two mid cards and keeping my 13s.

Finley.note: Alex's Eagle claim is contradicted by the table's reasoning, so I'm throwing at Alex. I'll throw two mid cards, H7 and D3, to secure the vote and bank some value if Farm wins.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle count rule was unclear: I wrote that my Eagle visit to Blair should give me nothing, and the table read it as including my own visit, which I never fully resolved. The dawn report's "visited by nobody else" wording also made the count easy to misread.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Drew's +1 was explained by my Turkey paying visitors, and the table worked it out from egg counts alone. Those cross-checks felt like real deduction.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports explicit about whether a player's own visit is counted, so the Eagle and Owl rules are not misread. I would also state the Turkey payout more clearly in the rules.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw my H4 at Blair and then let the table push me out as Eagle, when I should have revealed my Eagle visit's exact count earlier and pressed Blair's Floofer-like silence harder. Instead I should have pointed out the Eagle count rule sooner and defended myself with the dawn report before the vote.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visitor-counting rules were easy to misread under pressure, and several players, me included, argued about whether a player's own visit counts. Being confused also made my dawn report unreliable, so my Pigeon read was useless.
Blair.fun: Round 2's vote, where Alex's Hawk story and Casey's Turkey story clashed over the egg counts, was a satisfying puzzle to untangle.
Blair.change: I'd make dawn reports say who visited you and whether the report is confused, so players can cross-check egg counts without arguing over rule details.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I called CAW and threw at Alex, who was Farm, based on the Eagle count. I should have pressed harder on Ellis's Tit claim, which was the real contradiction.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey egg rules were the hardest to track, especially whether an Eagle counts its own visit and whether a Turkey's visitors gain eggs or the Turkey does. I also misstated the Eagle rule mid-day in round 3.
Casey.fun: Round 3, as the Meowfia Sphinx, I learned the Turkey was Drew, and our team eggsecuted the Farm Eagle, Alex, for a 19-point bank.
Casey.change: I would make dawn reports list visitors and egg sources explicitly, so players can check claims like the Eagle and Turkey counts without arguing over the rules.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I garbled my day speech and wrongly accused Ellis of lying about the Tit, when Ellis was honest. I would have stuck to a short, accurate story and pushed the Eagle count question instead.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Owl rules were hard to pin down: the Eagle counts the target's visitors, and the Owl only gets an egg if nobody else visits it. Several players, me included, argued the arithmetic from different readings, and it cost us time.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when I was the Sphinx and everyone built stories about Owl and Turkey eggs while I quietly steered the vote, and I still got an egg back on the consolation return.
Drew.change: Put each visitor count explicitly in the dawn report so Eagle, Owl and Turkey claims can be checked without anyone reconstructing the rule.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw a Wild at Casey, which wasted a vote; knowing the truth, I'd keep my real cards and push harder against Ellis, the Sphinx and real Meowfia threat.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visitor counts were hard to track, and I misread my own Tit egg as a hit when the +1 was really the Turkey payout. Casey's garbled "Meowfia... no, Farm" line also made it hard to read them.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when Drew refused to name an animal and our Farm throws of 7 cards won the round and banked 7 points. Watching the table pick apart each egg count was also a good puzzle.
Ellis.change: I'd make dawn reports list each visitor by name, so players can check Eagle and Owl counts without guessing what the rule includes.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Alex, a Farm player, on a count that was really the Turkey and Eagle confusion, when Casey was the Meowfia Sphinx. I should have thrown at Casey, whose odd garbled line was the stronger lead.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle and Owl egg counts were hard to pin down, since the dawn report counts only other visitors and it was unclear whether an Eagle counts its own visit. Several players, including me, misread the Turkey payout too.
Finley.fun: Round 1 went well: my Tit guess, the Turkey payout, and the table cross-checking eggs made the day feel like real deduction. Catching Drew as Meowfia felt good.
Finley.change: Make the dawn report state plainly whether a player's own visit counts toward their egg total, so Eagle and Owl claims can be checked without argument.
Finley.regret: In Round 3 I helped throw at Alex, a Farm Eagle, because Alex's count looked wrong, while Casey, the real Meowfia Sphinx, was steering the vote away from themselves. I would have questioned Casey's pushes harder and not joined the Alex vote so quickly.

review.title: Casey's Quiet Landslide
review.headline: A lone Sphinx hid behind a rules argument and banked 19 points.
review.summary: Round 1 went to Farm when Drew, the Sphinx, refused to name an animal and the table piled on. In round 2 the Meowfia pair of Blair and Ellis helped split the table, and Farm eggsecuted the Turkey Casey. In round 3 Alex's Eagle +0 looked like a lie to everyone. Farm threw at Alex, and Casey, the lone Meowfia, banked 19 points and won by 16.

rounds.recap: Drew, the Sphinx, dodged naming an animal. The Owl, Kookaburra and Falcon reports all fit together. Five players threw at Drew and Farm won easily.

Alex's Hawk +1 was ambiguous, since it also fit a Turkey payout. Casey's 'nobody visited me' looked like a lie, and Finley's Eagle count backed that. Meowfia Blair and Ellis nudged the table. Casey was eggsecuted as Farm and Meowfia won, but banked very little.

The table decided Alex's Eagle +0 was impossible, though Alex's report said Blair had no other visitors. Alex was eggsecuted as Farm. Casey was the only Meowfia. She won alone and banked 19 points with an 8, an 11 and a Wild.

highlights.text: Drew refused to name an animal and the whole table read that as a cat, while the Owl, Kookaburra and Falcon reports cross-checked cleanly.
Alex's +1 could be a Hawk hit or a Turkey payout, so the table split. Casey was eggsecuted as Farm.
Everyone treated Alex's Eagle +0 as proof of a lie, and Meowfia Casey joined the pile-on.
Casey's one winning throw took her from 10 to 29 points and decided the whole game.

confusions.what: Said the Tit hit proved Alex was a Pigeon, then reversed and admitted they had misread their own +1 as a Turkey payout.
Claimed an Owl lays an egg in its own nest, which is wrong. The Owl lays it in the target's nest.
Said Drew should be +2 after visiting a Turkey, ignoring that Drew's Sphinx visit was a different target. This was a shaky inference.
Said 'nobody visited me' while playing Turkey, though two players visited. She later said she meant only her nest count.
Said a Turkey gains an egg per visitor. A Turkey pays the visitors.
Gave a garbled opening claim ('Sphinx-less Dealer') and got the Eagle rule backwards, then flipped it.
Read their Tit +1 as a Pigeon hit, when it was the Turkey payout for visiting Drew.
Eagle +0 and 'nobody else visited' report. Alex concluded the Storyteller excluded his own visit, and the table rejected that.
Said Alex should be +1 as Eagle. Alex's own report is the only evidence, and the +0 fits either reading.

worked: Round 1 cross-checking: Owl, Falcon and Kookaburra reports corroborated each other, and the Sphinx's refusal to name an animal was a fair tell.
Hawk +1 versus Turkey payout in round 2 made a real ambiguity, and the table argued over it with real evidence.
The Wild card as a free vote gave players a cheap, readable throw in all three rounds.
The score-pile rule made the round 3 swing huge, so the leaderboard stayed live to the end.
problems: Dawn text is ambiguous. Alex's Eagle report said 'nobody else' and gave +0, so the table could not tell if the result was a bug or the rules. Fix: state the visitor list and the egg count plainly, and say whether the Eagle counts itself.

Winning throws score at full value, so one lone Meowfia can take a 19-point round. Casey's 10 to 29 jump ended the game after round 3. Consider capping banked cards per round or scaling the banked value.
Players kept misreading Turkey, Owl and Eagle direction. The rules text for who gets the egg is confusing. Add a short example for each role.
Most votes follow a single rules dispute rather than real evidence, so deduction was thin. Several players threw at whoever the table already named, with no real doubt.
Meowfia don't know each other, and in round 2 the pair barely coordinated. That is interesting, but Blair and Ellis banked almost nothing from the win, so a win as Meowfia felt pointless.
